headline: Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the importance of discerning wisdom
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the importance of discerning wisdom

08 SEP 2026 7:51AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting that a wise and discerning person should draw the essence from every branch of knowledge, whether great or small. He emphasised the importance of seeking and assimilating valuable wisdom from every source.

The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam-

“अणुभ्यश्च महद्भ्यश्च शास्त्रेभ्यः कुशलो नरः।

सर्वतः सारमादद्यात् पुष्पेभ्य इव षट्पदः॥”

The Subhashitam conveys that A wise and discerning person should draw the essence from every branch of knowledge, great or small, just as a bee gathers nectar from every flower. Likewise, one should seek out and assimilate the most valuable wisdom from every source.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

अणुभ्यश्च महद्भ्यश्च शास्त्रेभ्यः कुशलो नरः।

सर्वतः सारमादद्यात् पुष्पेभ्य इव षट्पदः॥ pic.twitter.com/tRxMbC7War

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) September 8, 2026

headline: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh inaugurates Day-Care Cancer Facility at Vidisha Medical College; says Tata Memorial enter (TMC) taking comprehensive cancer care closer to people
fullText:
Department of Atomic Energy

Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh inaugurates Day-Care Cancer Facility at Vidisha Medical College; says Tata Memorial enter (TMC) taking comprehensive cancer care closer to people

Rising cancer burden calls for expansion of cancer-care facilities beyond major metropolitan centres; India could see around 20 lakh new cases annually by 2030, says Dr Jitendra Singh

Dr Jitendra Singh calls for cooperation from citizens and society to check malpractices like food adulteration etc that may add to the Cancer burden:

TMC expanding cancer-care facilities at different levels across the country, from cancer treatment and radiation to prevention, early detection and training of State-level doctors

Vidisha cancer-care programme to progressively expand with trained doctors and nursing personnel, advanced diagnostics, radiotherapy and LINAC, cancer registries and palliative care

TMC’s national cancer-care network now spans 11 institutional units, while National Cancer Grid connects 300+ cancer centres; GMC Kathua also part of expanding regional cancer-care ecosystem

08 SEP 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today said that the rising cancer burden in the country calls for a sustained expansion of cancer-care facilities at different levels so that patients can access quality treatment closer to their homes. He said that the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), through Tata Memorial Centre (TMC), is working to take cancer-care capabilities to different parts of the country, with services ranging from cancer treatment and radiation to prevention, early detection, diagnosis and training of medical professionals.

Dr Jitendra Singh also called for cooperation from citizens and society to check malpractices like food adulteration etc that may add to the Cancer burden.

Dr. Jitendra Singh was speaking at the inauguration of the Day-Care Cancer Facility at Atal Bihari Vajpayee Government Medical College, Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh. Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Madhya Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Shri Rajendra Shukla were among the dignitaries present on the occasion. The facility is being developed with technical support from Tata Memorial Centre, Department of Atomic Energy, as part of a phased effort to strengthen cancer-care services at the medical college.

The Minister said that the Vidisha initiative should be seen as part of a larger national effort under which the Department of Atomic Energy, through Tata Memorial Centre, is developing cancer-care capabilities at different levels according to local requirements. “Somewhere it is cancer care, somewhere it is radiation, and we are also training State-level doctors in cancer management,” he said, stressing the need to take specialised cancer-care capabilities beyond major metropolitan centres.

The Vidisha programme began with a Cancer Gap Care Analysis undertaken by a multidisciplinary team of senior specialists from Tata Memorial Centre from June 5 to 7, 2026. The team comprised specialists in surgical, medical and radiation oncology, pathology and preventive care. During the same period, a large-scale cancer screening and awareness camp was organised in Vidisha. 586 cancer patients and 254 suspected cases were identified during the two-day screening programme, with arrangements made for appropriate further treatment and referral.

The Minister said that the day-care facility is the first step in a phased expansion of cancer-care services at Vidisha Medical College. Tata Memorial Centre has already provided a structured action plan covering equipment and drug procurement, medical oncology, surgical oncology, radiotherapy, pathology, community outreach, cancer registries and palliative care.

As part of the manpower-development component, two doctors from the Medicine Department and seven nursing officers from Vidisha have already completed dedicated oncology training at ACTREC, Mumbai. Training of surgeons and surgical staff from Vidisha at ACTREC, Kharghar, is scheduled to commence shortly, with the objective of enabling the institution to manage common surgical cancers locally.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that radiotherapy is another important component of the Vidisha cancer-care plan. The Government of Madhya Pradesh has announced construction of a radiotherapy facility at Government Medical College, Vidisha, with a Linear Accelerator (LINAC) facility expected to be commissioned within the next two to three years. This will provide patients from Vidisha and surrounding districts access to advanced radiation treatment closer to home.

The programme also provides for strengthening cancer diagnostics and pathology services. Tata Memorial Centre has provided a comprehensive list of Immunohistochemistry (IHC) and molecular markers required for accurate diagnosis and sub-typing of cancers. Pathology personnel from Vidisha are being prepared for specialised training at TMC, Mumbai, in oncopathology, IHC techniques and molecular diagnostics.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that cancer care cannot be limited to treatment after diagnosis and must also place strong emphasis on prevention and early detection. Tata Memorial Centre will work with the medical college towards establishing a centre of excellence for cancer prevention and early detection through education and research. Healthcare workers will also be trained in evidence-based strategies for reducing the cancer burden, with TMC supporting implementation and periodic monitoring.

The Vidisha programme will further strengthen local cancer data through the establishment of both a Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) and a Hospital-Based Cancer Registry (HBCR). These registries will generate local information on cancer incidence, stage at diagnosis and treatment outcomes, providing an evidence base for future planning and allocation of resources. Dedicated palliative-care services are also being developed, with doctors and nursing personnel to receive structured training in palliative medicine.

Putting the Vidisha initiative in the wider national context, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the scale of the cancer challenge makes it necessary to expand access to cancer care beyond a limited number of major centres. He referred to projections that India could see around two million new cancer cases annually by 2030, making expansion of prevention, early detection, diagnosis and treatment capacity increasingly important.

He said that the Department of Atomic Energy through Tata Memorial Centre has already created a substantial institutional network for cancer care. According to a March 2026 PIB release, TMC has established 11 hospital/institutional units across seven States, including centres in Mumbai, Kharghar-New Mumbai, Punjab, Varanasi, Visakhapatnam, Muzaffarpur and Guwahati.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that this institutional network is complemented by the National Cancer Grid (NCG), which has grown into a collaborative network of more than 380 cancer centres, research organisations, patient groups and professional bodies. The Grid supports quality improvement, standardisation, manpower training and cancer research, helping strengthen cancer services across the country.

The Minister said that the objective is to create a system in which the expertise and experience of established cancer centres can progressively support institutions in other parts of the country. TMC's existing network provides models for developing stronger regional linkages, while the National Cancer Grid provides a platform for technical inputs, standardisation, training, research and knowledge-sharing.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to the Government Medical College, Kathua, which is among the institutions where cancer-care capacity is being strengthened through collaboration with Tata Memorial Centre. The broader approach, he said, is to enable medical institutions outside the major metropolitan centres to progressively develop capabilities suited to the needs of their respective regions.

The Minister said that the cancer-care effort under DAE-TMC is therefore not limited to setting up standalone treatment facilities. It encompasses medical oncology, surgical oncology, radiation oncology, advanced pathology, prevention and early detection, cancer surveillance, palliative care and training of doctors and nursing personnel.

The Vidisha initiative reflects this integrated approach. Beginning with the day-care facility, the medical college is moving towards a broader cancer-care framework that will progressively bring together treatment, diagnostics, radiotherapy, trained manpower, prevention, early detection, cancer registries and palliative care under one coordinated programme.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the larger objective is to ensure that the benefits of India's growing cancer-care ecosystem reach patients closer to where they live, reducing the need for patients and their families to travel long distances for diagnosis and treatment.

The Vidisha facility, he said, marks another step in taking specialised cancer-care capabilities beyond major metropolitan centres and building a more accessible, decentralised and comprehensive cancer-care network across the country.

(Release ID: 2307824)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh inaugurated the Day-Care Cancer Facility at Atal Bihari Vajpayee Government Medical College, Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, as part of a phased expansion of cancer-care services by the Department of Atomic Energy through Tata Memorial Centre.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Inauguration date: 08 September 2026.
- Cancer Gap Care Analysis conducted June 5–7, 2026; two-day screening identified 586 cancer patients and 254 suspected cases.
- Two doctors and seven nursing officers completed oncology training at ACTREC, Mumbai; surgical staff training at ACTREC, Kharghar, scheduled to commence shortly.
- Radiotherapy Linear Accelerator (LINAC) facility expected to be commissioned within two to three years.
- Establishment of Population-Based and Hospital-Based Cancer Registries (PBCR and HBCR), palliative-care services, and pathology/IHC training planned.
- TMC’s network spans 11 institutional units across seven states; National Cancer Grid connects 300+ cancer centres, with GMC Kathua also part of the ecosystem.
- India projected to see around 20 lakh (two million) new cancer cases annually by 2030.

headline: IAF DRONATHON 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

IAF DRONATHON 2026

08 SEP 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi

IAF is organising Dronathon-2026 with an aim to offer domestic manufacturers to exhibit their capabilities and advancements in Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and Counter Unmanned Aerial Systems (CUAS). The event is designed to help stakeholders to witness emerging drone and counter drone technologies along with their operational demonstration and foster mutual learning.

The event is scheduled to take place at Pokhran range, Jaisalmer from 14 to 16 Sep 26. The event comprises of static display and live demonstrations. It will help to identify contemporary solutions and evaluate their combat effectiveness. Key areas of focus include surveillance and reconnaissance, autonomous operations, swarm technologies, and electronic warfare.

Aligning with the national vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. Dronathon-2026 aims to bolster the indigenous defence ecosystem by integrating industry experts, start-ups, and innovators. Through such initiatives, the IAF remains committed to building a technologically advanced, indigenous and future ready force capable of meeting security challenges in the rapidly changing operational environment.

headline: DFPD and FCI Sign MoU for FY 2026–27 to Strengthen Efficiency, Technology and Accountability in Foodgrain Management
fullText:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

DFPD and FCI Sign MoU for FY 2026–27 to Strengthen Efficiency, Technology and Accountability in Foodgrain Management

08 SEP 2026 3:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD) and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the Financial Year 2026–27 in New Delhi. The MoU establishes a comprehensive performance framework for FCI, with defined targets aimed at improving operational efficiency, strengthening accountability and accelerating modernisation in foodgrain management.

The MoU focuses on key areas including reduction of storage losses, optimal utilisation of storage capacity, improvement in logistics and supply chain management, and strengthening of quality control mechanisms. It also places emphasis on greater digitisation of business processes and adoption of modern Information Technology solutions to enhance efficiency, transparency and monitoring of FCI’s operations.

As part of the modernisation agenda, the MoU provides for capacity building and skill development initiatives for FCI employees, enabling the organisation to effectively adopt emerging technologies and contemporary systems of foodgrain management.

Established in 1965 under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, FCI plays a pivotal role in maintaining the country’s food security by undertaking procurement, storage, movement and distribution of foodgrains on behalf of the Government of India. Given the scale of public resources involved in its operations, efficient utilisation of food subsidy and continuous improvement in operational processes remain key priorities.

The MoU introduces a measurable and outcome-oriented approach to FCI’s functioning by linking its performance with clearly defined annual parameters. The framework is intended to promote greater efficiency in the utilisation of resources, strengthen transparency in operations and encourage adoption of technology-driven solutions across the organisation.

A proportion of the MoU targets has been linked to the performance of FCI’s depots through the Depot Darpan Portal, a web-based platform for assessing depot infrastructure and operational efficiency. Outcome- and target-based benchmarks have been incorporated to strengthen physical infrastructure, improve operational performance and promote continuous improvement across FCI depots.

The signing of the MoU reflects the Government’s continued commitment towards modernising the foodgrain management system and enhancing the efficiency and resilience of the country’s food security architecture. Through this performance-based framework, DFPD and FCI reaffirm their commitment to ensuring that food subsidy resources are utilised in a cost-effective and transparent manner while delivering greater value to the nation.

(Release ID: 2307810)

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lays foundation stones, inaugurates and dedicates to the Nation development projects worth more than ₹35,000 Crore In Vadodara, Gujarat
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lays foundation stones, inaugurates and dedicates to the Nation development projects worth more than ₹35,000 Crore In Vadodara, Gujarat

We are strengthening India's infrastructure to move people and goods faster, create new opportunities and power economic growth: PM

The Dedicated Freight Corridor is the lifeline of a rapidly developing India: PM

From chips to ships, India is now building a new manufacturing future: PM

08 SEP 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi laid foundation stones, inaugurated and dedicated to the Nation development projects worth more than ₹35,000 Crore in Vadodara, Gujarat. Extending warm greetings to the esteemed dignitaries, the Prime Minister commenced his address. He welcomed the citizens joining the monumental occasion both physically and via online mediums. "I welcome my brothers and sisters of Gujarat,” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the vibrant atmosphere at the Maharaja Sayajirao University ground, the Prime Minister celebrated the unique convergence of professionals from diverse fields gathering for a shared festival of progress. He expressed immense joy at witnessing such a unified celebration of development. "Everything is happening here simultaneously,” noted Shri Modi.

Dedicating infrastructure projects worth thousands of crores to accelerate national progress, the Prime Minister expressed deep appreciation for the exceptional cleanliness drive organized by the citizens of Vadodara to welcome him. He thanked the local population for their profound spirit of service during this festival of development. "Today I have come among you to give further momentum to the journey of a Viksit Bharat,” asserted Shri Modi.

Outlining the 'Saptadhara' (seven streams) resolution announced at the Red Fort, the Prime Minister emphasized the critical need for rapid connectivity through the Gati Shakti initiative, marking the historic completion of the 2800-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor. He praised Vadodara as the true city of Gati Shakti University where the final links of this massive project were connected. "This historic task for 21st-century India has been accomplished,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Showcasing the accelerated momentum post-2014, the Prime Minister celebrated the successful execution of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors which are now fundamentally transforming the commercial landscape. He noted that these networks are rapidly becoming the bedrock of the nation's commerce. "We gave it momentum and demonstrated it by completing the work of the 2800-kilometer corridor,” asserted Shri Modi.

Elaborating on the transformative impact of this new national lifeline, the Prime Minister detailed how separating passenger and freight traffic allows over 430 cargo trains to run daily, slashing a 30-hour truck journey to just 10-12 hours. He explained that covering 100 kilometers now takes less than half the previous time, saving fuel, reducing freight charges, and protecting the environment. "The investment was made on one track, but it yielded numerous benefits,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the profound agricultural benefits of the expanded logistics network, the Prime Minister explained how farmers across Eastern and Western India can now swiftly transport perishable goods to larger markets. He emphasized that sensitive items like seasonal flowers, vegetables, and fruits are finally reaching consumers and mandis right on time. "This has immensely benefited the farmers,” remarked Shri Modi.

Sharing a remarkable operational milestone on the new corridor, the Prime Minister praised the successful deployment of a double-stack container freight train from JNPT Port to Vadodara. He pointed out that this single train journey efficiently transported cargo equivalent to more than 250 trucks straight from Mumbai. "Large quantities of goods will now be able to reach from one corner of the country to another rapidly,” observed Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister underscored his administration's continuous rollout of new rail services that are finally penetrating isolated tribal regions across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. He celebrated a newly launched train that will immensely benefit commuters traveling to Chhota Udepur and Alirajpur. "Rail is now reaching those parts of India where it had not reached for decades,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the massive macroeconomic ripple effects of infrastructure development spanning roads, metros, airports, and gas pipelines, the Prime Minister cited the historic railway budget of over 2.75 lakh crore rupees as a primary engine for generating millions of employment opportunities. He explained that building houses for the poor and expanding ports naturally incubates new industries and businesses in the surrounding areas. "The expenditure happening on the modernization of the railways is creating thousands upon thousands of new jobs,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Transitioning to the manufacturing pillar of his 'Saptadhara' vision, the Prime Minister lauded Vadodara's 150-year legacy of industrial evolution from textiles to petrochemicals, and its massive growth as an MSME hub over the last two decades. He proudly acknowledged the city's crowning achievement as the birthplace of India's first domestically manufactured military transport aircraft. "The first flight of the C-295 aircraft has already seen the sky here,” remarked Shri Modi.

Illustrating the country's surging industrial capacity over the past decade, the Prime Minister presented robust statistics showcasing India's transformation into a major global manufacturer of modern railway coaches, wagons, and locomotive engines. He specified that since 2014, the nation has successfully produced 50,000 modern coaches and introduced nearly 2.5 lakh wagons to the railway network. "India has become a major manufacturer of rail coaches, metro coaches, and rail engines,” noted Shri Modi.

Championing the drive toward total self-reliance across critical supply chains, the Prime Minister highlighted the domestic production of solar PV modules which slashed previously exorbitant import costs and built a massive 200 GW capacity. He celebrated the success of the Kadana Dam floating solar project and the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which has empowered 55 lakh families nationwide, including 11 lakh in Gujarat, to become electricity producers and generate immense local employment. "India is now writing a new saga of manufacturing from chip to ship,” asserted Shri Modi.

Dismissing the echoes of lies propagated by detractors, the Prime Minister expressed deep faith in the youth who witnessed the government's intense focus across solar, wind, hydro, and nuclear sectors. He praised the younger generation for recognizing the massive strides being made in national development. "The youth of India walks with the roar of truth,” affirmed Shri Modi.'

Emphasizing the strategic necessity of a robust electric ecosystem to power emerging technologies like data centers and artificial intelligence, the Prime Minister confirmed that international agreements for uranium, critical minerals, and rare earth elements are being actively secured. He stated that creating this essential infrastructure is critical if the nation is to become a global superpower in AI. "All this hard work is being done solely to secure the future of the country's youth,” asserted Shri Modi.

Addressing the shifting paradigms of the modern global economy, the Prime Minister stressed that traditional degrees are no longer sufficient, prompting a comprehensive restructuring of the National Education Policy to prioritize continuous skill enhancement. He noted that teaching and training institutions are being entirely remolded to meet the evolving demands of the world. "It has become a massive necessity for the youth to possess skills and for those skills to be upgraded,” observed Shri Modi.'

Fulfilling a crucial commitment made from the Red Fort, the Prime Minister announced a landmark initiative to provide free coaching for competitive exams, aiming to alleviate the immense financial strain on poor and middle-class households. He assured that the administration will take direct responsibility for supporting the aspirations of students preparing for their careers. "The government itself will take care of the coaching of our youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.'

Recognizing artificial intelligence as a foundational capability transcending the IT sector, the Prime Minister unveiled plans for a massive national campaign to cultivate AI-proficient youth capable of driving innovations in agriculture, healthcare, and robotics. He emphasized that mastering these cutting-edge tools will boost manufacturing productivity and spark innovative startups. "We want our younger generation to be ready for AI,” asserted Shri Modi.

Concluding with a powerful call to action, the Prime Minister urged the nation to capitalize on this unprecedented demographic dividend, maintaining an unwavering focus on transforming the country by 2047. He ended his address by offering his best wishes for the ongoing development works. "We must relentlessly ensure India becomes developed,” affirmed Shri Modi.

The major increase in area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh (3.97 lakh ha), Jharkhand (0.98 lakh ha), Telangana (0.90 lakh ha), Rajasthan (0.57 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.38 lakh ha) etc. On the other hand, the major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Maharashtra (2.60 lakh ha), Karnataka (2.07 lakh ha), Odisha (0.61 lakh ha) etc. Overall, the increase in pulses area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial gains in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, which more than offset the declines reported in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Odisha.

Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals: About 181.39 lakh ha area coverage under Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals has been reported as compared to 182.48 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 1.09 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Karnataka (5.64 lakh ha), Maharashtra (2.41 lakh ha), Andhra Pradesh (0.62 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (0.24 lakh ha) etc. The higher area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (2.90 lakh ha), Chhattisgarh (1.69 lakh ha), Odisha (0.85 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.80 lakh ha), Bihar (0.72 lakh ha), Uttar Pradesh (0.63 lakh ha), Jharkhand (0.41 lakh ha), Uttarakhand (0.38 lakh ha), etc. Overall, the decline in area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Karnataka and Maharashtra, along with declines in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.

Oilseeds: About 191.99 lakh ha area coverage under oilseeds has been reported as compared to 193.06 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 1.07 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (2.23 lakh ha), Gujarat (1.93 lakh ha), Karnataka (0.37 lakh ha), etc. The higher area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh (2.91 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (1.14 lakh ha), etc. Overall, the decline in oilseed area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Rajasthan and Gujarat, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

Sugarcane: About 58.47 lakh ha area coverage under sugarcane has been reported as compared to 58.87 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.40 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Bihar (0.30 lakh ha), Uttarakhand (0.20 lakh ha), etc. The higher area coverage has been reported in Uttar Pradesh (0.36 lakh ha), Haryana (0.21 lakh ha), etc. Overall, the decline in sugarcane area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Bihar and Uttarakhand followed, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.

Jute & Mesta: About 6.34 lakh ha area coverage under Jute & Mesta has been reported as compared to 6.24 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing an increase of 0.10 lakh ha. The major increase in area coverage has been reported in Bihar (0.11 lakh ha), West Bengal (0.06 lakh ha), etc. On the other hand, the decrease in area coverage has been reported in Assam (0.07 lakh ha), Pradesh (0.01 lakh ha) etc., Overall, the increase in Jute & Mesta area is mainly attributable to higher coverage in Bihar and West Bengal, which have more than offset the decline reported in Assam and Andhra Pradesh.

Cotton: About 109.17 lakh ha area coverage under cotton has been reported as compared to 109.87 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.69 lakh ha. The major decrease in area coverage has been reported in Rajasthan (1.05 lakh ha), Haryana (0.90 lakh ha), Punjab (0.43 lakh ha), etc. On the other hand, higher area coverage has been reported mainly in Telangana (1.14 lakh ha), Gujarat (0.66 lakh ha), etc.. Overall, the decline in cotton area coverage is mainly attributable to substantial reductions in Rajasthan and Haryana, followed by declines in Punjab, which have more than offset the gains recorded in Telangana and Gujarat.

headline: President of India to Present 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat on 22 September
fullText:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting

President of India to Present 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat on 22 September

08 SEP 2026 1:55PM by PIB Delhi

The 72nd National Film Awards will be presented by the President of India on 22 September 2026 at Ekta Nagar (Kevadia), Gujarat. The ceremony will bring together filmmakers, actors, technicians and other artists from across the country to celebrate outstanding achievements in Indian cinema for the year 2024.

Instituted in 1954, the National Film Awards are country’s most prestigious honours for excellence in cinema. Over seven decades, the Awards have recognised outstanding creative and technical achievements across feature films, non-feature films and writing on cinema, while reflecting the rich linguistic, cultural and regional diversity of Indian filmmaking.

In a major policy initiative, it has been decided by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting to hold National Film Awards in various parts of the country taking it beyond the National Capital. The ceremony at Ekta Nagar this year will bring together cinematic talent from across India, embody the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.

The 72nd National Film Awards celebrate this diversity across a wide range of languages, genres and cinematic forms. ‘Article 370’ will be honoured as the Best Feature Film. ‘Bhangaar’ has been adjudged the Best Non-Feature Film and ‘Ram-Nami’ was chosen as the Best Documentary by the Jury. Mammootty for ‘Bramayugam’ and Kartik Aaryan for ‘Chandu Champion’ have been announced the Best Actor in a Leading Role award, while Yami Gautam will be honoured as Best Actress in a Leading Role for ‘Article 370’. Randeep Hooda will receive the Best Debut Director award for ‘Swatantrya Veer Savarkar’.

The Awards also recognise excellence in films across languages and forms, including Marathi, Santhali, Tamil, Malayalam, Telugu, Kannada, Tulu and Garhwali, among others. Several films, including ‘Kalki 2898 AD’, ‘Amaran’, ‘Pushpa: The Rule Part-02’, ‘Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3’ and ‘Stree 2’, will also receive honours in various categories. For the first time, a Santhali film will be honoured in the Non-Feature Film section of the National Film Awards.

In the Best Writing on Cinema category, Sanjeev Shrivastava has been announced as Best Film Critic award. The Best Book on Cinema award will be given to ‘Naaniruvude Nimagaagi Naadiruvude Nanagaagi: Kannada Cinemada Thathva matthu Rajakeeya’ (I Stand for You, the State Stands for Us: Political and Philosophical Dimensions of Kannada Cinema) written by Dr. Pradeep Kenchanuru and published by Mirror Pusthaka.

Mahesh Kumar/Vivek Vishwash

headline: Progress and Success in the Coal Sector: MCL’s Transformative Journey Since 2014
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

Progress and Success in the Coal Sector: MCL’s Transformative Journey Since 2014

08 SEP 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian coal sector has witnessed a remarkable transformation since 2014, driven by a series of well-conceived policy and structural reforms of the Government of India aimed at enhancing transparency, efficiency, technology adoption, infrastructure development, ease of operations and energy security. These reforms have created an enabling environment for faster decision-making, modernisation of mining operations, improved logistics and higher productivity. Their impact is reflected in the coal sector achieving the landmark 1 Billion Tonne (BT) level of domestic coal production well ahead of the targeted timeline, significantly strengthening India’s energy security and reducing dependence on imported coal.

Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) represents one of the most compelling success stories of this transformation. From 23 MT of production in 1992-93, MCL has grown into India’s largest coal-producing company and has sustained more than 200 MT of both production and dispatch for three consecutive years. Its production growth accelerated to around 9% CAGR during FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26, compared with 6.7% during FY 1992-93 to FY 2020-21. This achievement reflects the combined impact of progressive policy reforms, modern mine planning, technology, infrastructure, operational efficiency and the commitment of MCL’s workforce.

The success of MCL, however, extends far beyond production and dispatch. The company has achieved its highest-ever profitability and remains one of the principal contributors to the profits of Coal India Limited, while making a substantial contribution to the Government exchequer. Its operations also generate extensive direct and indirect livelihood opportunities, with more than 22,000 regular employees, over 27,000 contractual workers and a large ecosystem of transportation and allied activities.

A particularly important dimension of this transformation is its human and social impact. Contractual workers associated with MCL benefit from wages aligned with the recommendations of the High Power Committee, which are higher than statutory minimum wages, along with social-security and welfare measures including CMPF, medical facilities and educational support. The CLAMP portal has enabled digital management of contractual manpower data, bringing greater transparency and accountability. Local communities have benefited through employment opportunities, engagement of cooperative societies in coal loading and transportation, and support extended to Project Affected Persons.

MCL’s commitment to community development and CSR is equally significant. It is among the highest CSR contributors in Odisha as well as among CIL subsidiaries. Its interventions encompass healthcare, education, drinking water, nutrition, sports, skill development and rural infrastructure. The construction of the Medical College and Hospital at Talcher, involving an investment of about ₹500 crore, along with continued annual financial support of around ₹60–80 crore, represents a major investment in public healthcare; the institution has also received approval for PG courses. Similarly, MCL-funded CSR support enabled the establishment of the first Government cardiac-care hospital at Jharsuguda. Piped drinking-water projects across the four districts in its command area and aspirational districts, support to AIIMS Bhubaneswar and Burla Medical College, schools, classrooms, smart classes, girls’ hostels, sports complexes and other community assets demonstrate that the benefits of coal mining extend well beyond the mine boundary.

The transformation is equally visible in technology, environment and logistics. More than 99% of MCL’s coal production is now through Surface Miner technology, which substantially reduces drilling, blasting, crushing, dust and other environmental disturbances. MCL is further investing around ₹10,000 crore in 19 First Mile Connectivity projects, about ₹6,500 crore in rail infrastructure and around ₹2,150 crore in concrete internal transportation roads and coal corridors. These initiatives are aimed at enhancing evacuation efficiency, reducing dependence on road transportation and minimising the environmental footprint. The company has already invested substantially in rail and FMC infrastructure, with nearly 70% of dispatch being undertaken through rail mode. Its pioneering Rail-Sea-Rail (RSR) multimodal logistics system further strengthens supply-chain efficiency and enables reliable coal supply to consumers across coastal regions.

MCL’s contribution also reaches the wider regional economy through tourism and heritage development, including initiatives around Hirakud, mine museums, waterfront development, ropeways and mine tourism at Orient Mine in the IB Valley. Community engagement has also been strengthened through initiatives such as the Bhubaneswar Half Marathon, which attracted around 6,000 participants, and the Hirakud–Sambalpur Half Marathon, which witnessed participation exceeding 10,000.

Today, MCL supplies coal across 16 States to power utilities, captive and independent power plants, cement, sponge iron and other industries. Its sustained performance has therefore become an important pillar of India’s energy security and industrial growth.

MCL’s journey demonstrates that the success of coal-sector reforms cannot be measured merely in tonnes of coal produced. It is a story of higher productivity, stronger profitability, better logistics, technological advancement, environmental responsibility, worker welfare, community development and nation-building. The transformation achieved since 2014 provides a powerful example of how progressive policy reforms, institutional responsiveness, modern technology and committed human resources can convert the immense potential of India’s coal sector into tangible economic and social value.

As India progresses towards a developed and energy-secure economy, MCL remains committed to carrying forward this momentum—producing and delivering more, efficiently and responsibly, while ensuring that the benefits of its growth reach its employees, communities, consumers and the nation at large.

headline: PM-SETU Strengthens Industry-Led ITI Transformation; 5th National Steering Committee Approves SIPs Worth ₹735.70 Crore
fullText:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

PM-SETU Strengthens Industry-Led ITI Transformation; 5th National Steering Committee Approves SIPs Worth ₹735.70 Crore

Approval raises cumulative PM-SETU investment to ₹2,171 crore across 9 ITI clusters, accelerating the creation of modern, industry-led and future-ready ITIs nationwide

08 SEP 2026 1:25PM by PIB Delhi

The 5th National Steering Committee (NSC) meeting of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) was held yesterday under the chairpersonship of the Smt Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).

The meeting was attended by Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General, Directorate General of Training (DGT); Smt. G.Madhumita Das, Addl Secretary and FA, Smt Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, MSDE; senior officials from the Ministry and State Governments; representatives from multilateral development banks; and industry partners.

In a significant step towards accelerating the transformation of India’s Industrial Training Institute (ITI) ecosystem, the National Steering Committee approved Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs) with an aggregate project outlay of ₹735.70 crore for ITI clusters in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Telangana.

The approvals further strengthen the industry-led approach of PM-SETU, with industry and institutional partners supporting the modernisation of ITI infrastructure, introduction of future-ready courses and closer alignment of training programmes with evolving industry requirements.

These approvals take the total sanctioned investment under PM-SETU to ₹2,171 crore across 9 ITI clusters further accelerating the creation of modern, industry-led and future-ready ITIs across the country.

₹735.70 Crore Investment Across Three ITI Clusters

The 5th NSC approved the following Strategic Investment Plans:

Rajasthan – ₹241.00 crore

The NSC approved the SIP submitted by M/s H.G. Infra Engineering Limited (HGIEL) for the Bhiwadi ITI cluster.

The cluster comprises Government ITI Bhiwadi as the Hub, with Government ITI Alwar, Government ITI Neemrana, Government ITI Tijara and Government ITI Kishangarh Bas as Spokes.

Telangana – ₹254.30 crore

The NSC approved the Strategic Investment Plan submitted by M/s ZEN Technologies Limited for the Medchal ITI cluster, which had earlier been deferred during the 4th NSC meeting for want of clarifications on operational and financial aspects.

The cluster comprises Government ITI Medchal as the Hub, with Government ITI Alwal, Government ITI Shameerpet, Government ITI Kukunoorpally and Government ITI Siddipet as Spokes.

Following detailed clarifications from the Anchor Industry Partner on course structure, financial calculations, eligibility, documentation and civil works, the Committee found the responses satisfactory and approved the SIP.

Uttar Pradesh – ₹240.40 crore

The Committee approved the SIP submitted by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) for the Meerut ITI cluster.

The cluster comprises Government ITI, Saket, Meerut as the Hub, with Government ITI Ghaziabad, Government ITI Hapur, Government ITI Gautam Buddha Nagar and Government ITI Baghpat as Spokes.

Industry Partnerships Driving ITI Modernisation

The approval of these SIPs marks another important milestone in the implementation of PM-SETU, which seeks to transform Government ITIs through an industry-led Hub-and-Spoke cluster model.

The approved plans provide for investments in infrastructure modernisation, upgradation of existing trades, introduction of new long-term and short-term courses, and strengthening of operational capabilities. The SIPs have been evaluated and recommended by the respective State Steering Committees before being placed before the National Steering Committee.

The three approved SIPs represent a combined project outlay of ₹735.70 crore, further deepening collaboration between the Government, State Governments and industry partners to create modern, industry-responsive and future-ready ITIs.

The approvals are expected to strengthen the capacity of ITIs to provide young people with skills aligned to emerging technologies, changing industry requirements and evolving employment opportunities.

A significant milestone was achieved during the meeting with the signing of the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA) among H.G. Infra Engineering Limited, the Government of Rajasthan and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (Government of India). The signing in the presence of Shri Sandeep Verma, Addl Chief Secretary – Dept of Skill Employment and Entrepreneurship, (Govt of Rajasthan) marks the formal commencement of implementation activities for the Bhiwadi ITI Cluster under PM-SETU and makes Rajasthan the first state in the country to execute an SHA under the scheme.

The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India aimed at transforming the ITI ecosystem through industry partnerships, modern infrastructure, upgraded training programmes and improved employability outcomes.

The scheme adopts an industry-led, cluster-based approach in which a Hub ITI is supported by a network of Spoke ITIs, enabling coordinated investment, modernisation and delivery of industry-relevant skills.

(Release ID: 2307775)

The approvals advance the government’s initiative to modernize ITIs through industry partnerships, infrastructure upgrades, and future-ready training programs.

Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister shares an article on Poshan initiatives and strengthening the Anganwadi system

08 SEP 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi

headline: Round 1 of Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects Concludes with Overwhelming Response Receiving Seven Applications from Leading Public and Private Sector Companies
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

Round 1 of Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects Concludes with Overwhelming Response Receiving Seven Applications from Leading Public and Private Sector Companies

NTPC, Adani Enterprises, Talcher Fertilisers, Gallantt Ispat and Shyam Sel & Power Limited Among Applicants as India's Flagship Coal Gasification Push Gathers Momentum

08 SEP 2026 11:39AM by PIB Delhi

The Round 1 of the ₹37,500 crore Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects has closed to an overwhelming response from industry, with seven (7) applications received from some of India's largest corporate houses and premier public sector undertakings, decisively vindicating the Ministry of Coal's confidence in the scheme. The response underscores growing industry confidence in coal gasification as a key pillar of India's energy security, import substitution and industrial development strategy.

The applications received under the first round are as follows:

Sl. No. | Applicant | End Product(s)

1 | NTPC Limited (1 Project) | Synthetic Natural Gas

2 | Adani Enterprises Limited (3 Projects) | Urea

3 | Gallantt Ispat Limited (1 Project) | Direct Reduced Iron and Syngas

4 | Shyam Sel & Power Limited (1 Project) | Syngas

5 | Talcher Fertilisers Limited (1 Project) | Urea

“When we said reports of ‘no takers’ were premature, we were confident that industry would respond and it has, decisively. Seven applications in the very first round, including from some of India’s largest industrial houses and public sector undertakings, are a clear vote of confidence in the scheme and in India’s coal gasification mission. The market has spoken, and it has spoken loudly.”- said Shri Alok Kumar Singh, Advisor (Projects), Ministry of Coal.

The coal and lignite gasification projects are large-scale, capital-intensive investments that require extensive preparatory work, including pre-feasibility studies, technology assessments, environmental considerations and detailed financial planning. The submission of seven applications within the first round is a testament to the seriousness with which industry has engaged with the scheme since the Request for Proposal was issued on 7 July 2026. These projects have the potential to contribute significantly to the development of a robust domestic coal gasification ecosystem, with eight gasification projects already under implementation under the earlier ₹8,500 crore Financial Incentive Scheme.

Scheme Background

The Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects was approved by the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, on 13th May 2026, with a total financial outlay of ₹37,500 crore. The scheme is designed to:

Promote the conversion of domestic coal and lignite into higher-value products such as syngas, methanol, ammonia, urea and hydrogen.

Reduce India's dependence on imports of LNG, urea, ammonia and methanol, which together accounted for approximately ₹2.77 lakh crore in imports during FY 2024-25.

Support the national objective of achieving 100 million tonnes of coal gasification capacity by 2030, including the development of 75 million tonnes of capacity under the scheme.

Catalyse investments estimated at ₹2.5-3 lakh crore and generate substantial direct and indirect employment opportunities across the value chain.

The scheme builds on the National Coal Gasification Mission and the ₹8,500 crore scheme approved in January 2024, under which eight projects are currently under implementation.

Applications received under Round 1 will now undergo detailed evaluation in accordance with the scheme guidelines and the RFP.

The Ministry further announced the opening of Round 2 of the scheme from 8 September 2026. In accordance with the RFP, the application windows will continue to open at two-month intervals, providing regular opportunities for eligible entities to participate. Several prospective applicants are presently at advanced stages of project preparation and are expected to submit proposals in forthcoming rounds.

The Ministry appreciates the participation of all applicants and their confidence in the scheme. It remains committed to accelerating the development of coal gasification technologies in India, strengthening energy security and import substitution, and positioning the country as a global leader in clean coal technologies.
